The number of significant places retained in the rourded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

2.3 Steps and Grooves - The pirns shall have steps or grooves or both on the body; the shape and number of which shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller. In case of pirns with steps, the edges of the steps shall be rounded off. 2.4 Shield - The shield ( s ), if prescribed by the buyer, shal. be rigidly fixed and should be punched ( at equal distance ) at least at :`our places at the bottom and two places at the top of the pirn. 2.4.1 Metal shield shall be made of either tin plate having minimum thickness of 0'3 15 mm or sheet of any other metal with suitable anti-rust treatment of the thickness as agreed to between the buyer andthe seller subject to a tolerance of f 0'03 mm. 2.5 Finish - The pirris shall be enamelled or varnished as igreed to between the buyer and the seller and shall have smooth finish. 2.6 Freedom from Defects - The pirns shall be visually fpe from barkpocket, checks, cracks, gum ducts, honeycombing, knot, spits and any other defect which is likely to affect the life or usefulness of the pirns. For the description of various types of defects, see IS : 7(Y-1976+ and IS : 3364 (Part 2 )-1976t. 3. 3.1.2 Fitting Dimensions
The pirns shall fit on the spindle in such a way that the distance between the bottom of the pirn and the top of the wtrarve ( E in Fig. 2 ) is 10 f 2 mm. When the pirn is correctly seated on the spindle, the radial clearance between the blade of the spindle and the inside of pirn shall be 0'25 + 0'05 mm. - 0'00 3.2 Concentricity - The pirns shall be concentric. However, eccentricity ofpirns shall not exceed 0'5 mm at a position 20 mm below the top of pirn and 0'75 mm at a position 20 mm above the bottom of the'pirn, when tested by the mothod given in A-l. 3.3 Tackiness - The pirns shall not tend to stick to the thumb and the impression, if any, can be wiped OR wrth dry cotton when tested by the method given in A-2. shall be moisture-resistant. 3.4 Resistant to Mojsture - Pins However, enamelled pirns shall not absorb more than 3'5 percent and varnished pirns not more than 7 percent moisture, when tested by the method prescribed in A-3. 3.5 Res,istanco to Steam - The enamel show any sign of tackiness and cracking given in A-4. 6 coating on the pirns shall not when tested by the method

use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions ot `the NOTE -The Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard to comply with the conveys the assurance that they have been produced requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards,

METHOD A-l. CONCENTRICITY

A-l.1 On a suitable bobbin tester, mount a spindle (having eccentricity not more than 0'05 mm ) such that at its top, the let-on of a pirn may be expected to grip the spindle and at the base of the pirn there is a clearance of at least 1'5 mm between the blade of the spindle and the inside diameter of the pirn (see Note in A-l.2 ).

A-l.2 Take a pirn out of the test sample, fit. it on the spindle, revolve it slowly and determine the eccen.tricity of the pirn at a position 20 mm below the top of the pirn and at a positidn 20 mm above the bottom of thz pirn. Note the eccentricity, if any, at these two positions.
